chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman from Abd Allah ibn Sinan from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Pre-emption (shuf'ah) is only for two partners as long as they have not divided the property; but if they become three, then none of them has pre-emption.

key_terms.الشُّفْعَةُ: Pre-emption, the right of a co-owner to buy out the share of another partner before an outsider.
key_terms.ثَلَاثَةً: Three, the number of partners that nullifies the right of pre-emption in this ruling.
key_terms.لِشَرِيكَيْنِ: For two partners, indicating the specific condition of partnership count.
key_terms.يَتَقَاسَمَا: They divide, referring to the partition of the co-owned property.

ai.seo_question: When does the right of pre-emption (shuf'ah) cease to apply among co-owners?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* delineates the specific condition for the right of pre-emption (*shuf'ah*), restricting it to partnerships of exactly two owners to prevent the complexity of multiple claims. Once a third partner joins, the right is extinguished for all, reflecting the Shia juristic preference for simplicity in co-ownership disputes and avoiding the procedural complications of multiple simultaneous pre-emptors. This ruling underscores the practical application of property rights in early Islamic society, prioritizing clear title transfer over extended pre-emptive claims.
